# Auth verification storage

Auth owns verification policy, persistence ports, the direct authenticated Tarantool adapter, and `scripts/tarantool` schema/bootstrap. Infrastructure runs the same identity-store engine, volume, and endpoints (`identity-store:3301`; native `127.0.0.1:3301`). Auth connects using the configured identity runtime principal and opaque secret. There is no verification HTTP provider or Infrastructure API.

The runtime principal has session access and execute access only to `auth_verification` and `auth_verification_ready`. It has no EVAL, arbitrary CALL, direct space, or schema privileges. The closed functions run under a non-login verification owner with rights limited to the five verification spaces and read access to their migration ledger. Server-start local bootstrap owns migration administration and narrows old runtime universe grants. Authentication errors and driver diagnostics never expose tuple material.

`auth_verification(action,args)` accepts the eight declared operations: signup start/resend/legacy verify/recoverable consume, email start/verify, reset start/verify. Each executes validation and mutations in one `box.atomic` transaction. Code replacement, consumption, code lookup collision reservation, attempt increments, and receipt binding serialize across all Auth instances. Four-digit codes use cryptographic randomness; allocation failure fails closed. No code delivery adapter is added by this migration.

Signup recovery preserves canonical operation UUID, normalized email, provider SHA256 length-framed email/code binding, original bcrypt hash, and frozen `created_at + signup hard TTL`. Retry by the same operation recovers that exact receipt before expiry. Other bindings fail. Legacy verification cannot recover receipts. Auth's existing PostgreSQL reservation/principal ownership and terminal CAS remain independent durable boundaries; required User/RBAC acknowledgements precede token issuance. Password signin repairs owned verified pending signup; code replay after terminal completion fails. This is not a distributed database transaction.

Migration IDs 001–003, ledger `ms_go_tarantool_schema_migrations`, existing tuple formats, and index repair history remain unchanged. Migration 004 adds functions without dropping, truncating, reformatting, or rewriting existing data. Load `scripts/tarantool/init.lua` locally on server startup; it reloads functions and applies migrations repeatably. Running code never migrates remotely. There is no down migration.

One Lua cleanup fiber scans verification state atomically every minute. Code expiry prevents use; hard TTL bounds retained proofs. Receipt expiry remains frozen despite later configuration changes. Email-change code lookup cleanup verifies its UUID owner. Defaults are five-minute code TTL and 24-hour hard TTL. Auth duration settings and server cleanup integer-second settings must agree. Password reset shares Auth email TTL policy.

Legacy `user` and `sandbox` identity-store records remain retained, without mutation or cleanup. The old service constructed presence logic without invoking it; its legacy sandbox only had cleanup wired, with no externally reachable mutations. Their retired interfaces are not moved into Auth. Legacy presence belongs to User and legacy sandbox state to Sandbox if future restoration is needed; retention is indefinite pending an explicit owner-approved data policy. Modern Sandbox owns its independent sandbox-store `sandboxes` and workspace state; stores are never merged.

Real verification tests use `T16_DIRECT_VERIFICATION=true` and explicit owned loopback runtime and separate fixture credentials. Fixture reads/writes operate only on synthetic run-prefixed test identities; runtime never obtains those permissions. Integration tests cover independent connections, atomic consumption, replay, receipt recovery, collisions, expiry, resend, and production PostgreSQL/User/RBAC signup recovery. Skipped tests are not runtime evidence.

Coordinator restart acceptance runs `TestActualVerificationRestart` twice with `AUTH_VERIFICATION_RESTART_PHASE=seed|resume` and an absolute `AUTH_VERIFICATION_RESTART_STATE_FILE` private fixture path. The coordinator restarts the same disposable store/volume between phases. State is created exclusively with 0600 permissions and contains sensitive fixture proof/credential bindings; never publish or log it. Resume reconstructs the adapter and verifies the exact frozen receipt, retained live pending proof, replay/conflicting owner denial, and expired proof denial. `AUTH_VERIFICATION_RESTART_LEGACY_COUNTS=true` inventories retained legacy record counts when the separate fixture principal has read-only access to `user`/`sandbox`; resume compares those counts. Runtime remains unable to read those spaces.

Cleanup acceptance uses the coordinator-only `test/integration/fixtures/verification_cleanup_seed.lua`, loaded locally after production bootstrap on a disposable store. Explicit `AUTH_VERIFICATION_CLEANUP_FIXTURE_ENABLED=true` and a stable synthetic `AUTH_VERIFICATION_CLEANUP_PREFIX` within `T16_RUN_PREFIX` are required. It atomically seeds 1,205 expired records per verification kind, reverse indexes, live verification sentinels, and old legacy presence/sandbox sentinels. A separate fixture marker records the committed inventory; repeated startup with the same prefix never reseeds or overwrites records. Grant the fixture principal read-only access to that marker and the verification/legacy spaces. `TestActualVerificationCleanup` only reads those fixtures and waits up to 75 seconds for the production minute fiber. It checks complete removal beyond 1,000 records, preserves a live reverse mapping sharing an expired record's code, and compares retained tuples exactly. No cleanup trigger, clock override, remote administration, or production fixture hook is introduced.
